title: Quantile-driven Guardrails and Hierarchical Fallback Broker
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Background:
Redwood needs a resilient, predictable way to protect downstream dependencies (model variants, third-party tokenizers, embedding services) and tenant workloads when regional capacity or dependency health degrades. Existing per-path breakers are brittle: they use static error rates or single-threshold trips and often cause noisy cascades across regions. We need a unified controller that: 1) computes adaptive trip points from signal quantiles and EWMA, 2) supports hierarchical fallback policies (model variant -> cached reply -> degraded-mode stub), and 3) enforces tenant-prioritized shedding to preserve SLOs for high-priority customers during incidents.

Goals:
- Implement quantile-driven thresholds for breaker trips (p50/p95/p99) plus EWMA stabilization windows to avoid sensitivity to short spikes.
- Support per-dependency, per-model, and per-tenant breakers with inheritance: defaults at dependency level can be overridden by model, then by tenant.
- Implement a "Fallback Broker" that routes traffic to safe alternatives in priority order, accounting for regional availability and routing cost (latency/cost).
- Provide deterministic, observable state transitions and playbook hooks for ops (dry-run, staging canaries, automatic rollback).

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement cross-region capacity autoscaling. That is tracked in Reliability-Orchestration:scaling epics.
- We are not changing SLO definitions in this ticket; we consume SLOs provided by SLO-Team configs.
design_notes:
Signals used:
- latency quantiles (p50/p95/p99) computed per-minute and per-tenant where feasible
- 5xx error rate and model-specific inference error signals
- queue length/backpressure (requests waiting for GPU token)
- token-per-second throughput

Threshold synthesis:
- Baseline threshold = 95th-percentile observed under healthy windows (last 72h excluding incidents).
- Adaptive trip threshold = max(baseline * 1.3, EWMA(latency, alpha=0.25) * q_factor) where q_factor is derived from p95/p99 ratio to reflect tail heaviness.
- For errors, use a dual-signal: trip when both (error_rate > error_threshold) AND (p95 latency > latency_threshold) for a given window to avoid false trips on brief error bursts.

Breaker state machine (simplified):
- CLOSED: normal pass-through.
- SOFT-TRIP: temporarily divert a percentage of traffic to fallback (sampled shed), continue monitoring.
- OPEN: majority of traffic rerouted to fallback; periodic probes allowed to check recovery.
- COOLING: recently recovered; traffic ramps back via token-budget.

Hysteresis and safety windows:
- Minimum open duration = 30s.
- Cooling window = 5m with linear ramp of pass-through tokens.
- Circuit-lock: when a breaker opens for more than 10m, it escalates to an incident-tagged mode and notifies Ops.

Fallback Broker policy resolution order (per-request):
1) Tenant pinned variant if healthy and compatible
2) Regional-compatible model variant (lower-cost quantized variant)
3) Cached response (prefix/KV cache) if cache-allowed and TTL valid
4) Degraded-mode stub: deterministic short-text fallback + structured response indicating partial result
5) Reject with structured 503 + guidance (retry-after, alternative route token)

Tenant-priority shedding:
- Each tenant has a budget score (derived from committed capacity + SLAs). During shedding, the controller allocates tokens proportionally to budget and then applies priority caps. Low-priority tenants see earlier SOFT-TRIP sampling and lower recovery ramps.

Observability:
- Per-breaker metrics: state, uptime, open_count, sample_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, error_rate.
- Traces include breaker decision tags and fallback path chosen.
- Synthetic litmus tests: per-region SLO smoke generator that triggers predictable transitions for validation.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (spike & prototype, 2 weeks):
- Spike: implement quantile ingestion in metrics aggregator; prototype threshold computation in python.
- Lightweight runtime hook: add a 'broker' decision point after routing but before enqueue.
- Canary in staging (internal traffic) with dry-run.

Phase 2 (runtime integration, 3 weeks):
- Implement full state machine in routing service (go).
- Add tenant budget store to control plane; API for ops to adjust budgets and pin fallbacks.
- Implement fallback broker resolution against model catalog.

Phase 3 (rollout & hardening, 2 weeks):
- Canary to 5% production traffic for non-critical models.
- Add dashboards, alerts, and runbook.
- Post-incident review simulation and iterate thresholds.

API/Config surfaces:
- control-plane: /breaker-policies (CRUD), /tenant-budget (PATCH), /fallback-order (per model/tenant)
- runtime config flags: hysteresis windows, token-buckets, sample-seed for deterministic sampling

Backward compatibility:
- Default policies mirror current static thresholds; teams can opt-in to adaptive quantile mode via control-plane flag.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive thresholds computed and stored for at least 90% of active dependencies
Runtime enforces hierarchical fallback ordering and routes >=95% of fallback-bound requests as per policy
No more than 2% unexpected customer-facing 503s during 5% canary traffic for two weeks
Dashboards show breaker state, latency quantiles, and tenant budget utilization
Runbook validated: SRE can force-close/open and change budget with <2 minutes of latency
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Overly aggressive synthetic thresholds cause client-visible degradation. Mitigation: conservative default multipliers and a dry-run period with telemetry comparison.

Risk: Complexity of per-tenant state may increase memory footprint in routing plane. Mitigation: use hierarchical defaults, LRU eviction for cold tenants, and push heavy computations to control plane.

Risk: Fallback paths returning degraded content could violate downstream contracts. Mitigation: fallback broker respects schema and sets a 'degraded:true' response header; clients can opt-in to accept degraded outputs.

2026-03-03 - Design review notes from Carlos O.: prefer EWMA alpha=0.2 for p95 smoothing; flagged tenant budget API auth model (security team).
2026-03-08 - Implementing runtime state machine; initial Go prototype passes unit tests. Submitted internal RFC for breaker telemetry schema.
2026-03-12 - QA: staging canary dry-run running for 72h. Noted two false soft-trips on a model with bursty workloads; adjusting q_factor heuristics.
